description: I'm a solo developer from Sri Lanka passionate about AI, software engineering, and science. I enjoy experimenting with emerging technologies and turning ambitious ideas into working products. For NASA Space Apps 2026, I combined these interests to build Revealiã, making Earth science investigation more accessible through AI. I believe in learning by building, challenging conventional approaches, and turning curiosity into something tangible.
summary:
Revealiã makes Earth science investigation accessible to everyone, from students to curious members of the public. Finding datasets, accessing scientific data, analysing it, and interpreting results often requires specialised knowledge.

Simply ask a question, such as "Is the Amazon becoming more vulnerable to drought?", and investigate it alongside Revealiã, your AI research companion. It helps discover datasets, retrieve NASA and NOAA data, and perform scientific analysis. You can change variables, explore alternative datasets, try different methods, and ask follow-up questions.

Unlike ordinary conversational AI, Revealiã conducts actual investigations using real data and computational analysis. Explore the evidence, share cases, and download reports as PDFs or datasets as CSV files.

Revealiã also offers an open MCP server, allowing compatible AI assistants to access its scientific capabilities.
details:
What is Revealiã

Revealiã is a free, AI-powered Earth science investigation platform that helps anyone explore whether, how, and why our planet is changing. It brings scientific data, computational analysis, interactive exploration, and learning together in one place.

It brings together four core components:

  • Investigate: Turn a question into an actual scientific investigation. Ask something like "How have nitrogen dioxide levels changed across major south asian cities?" and an AI agent identifies the locations, discovers relevant NASA and NOAA datasets, retrieves live data, and performs statistical analysis. Watch the globe zoom to your area of interest, charts populate as results arrive, and follow an evidence-backed investigation revealing what changed, where, by how much, and whether the observed trend is statistically significant. Explore the investigation as it unfolds, change variables, try alternative datasets and analytical methods, and dig deeper into the findings.
  • Explore: Discover Earth through an interactive 3D globe featuring NASA satellite imagery and environmental data layers. Explore different parts of the planet, move through historical imagery, and watch environmental changes unfold over time.
  • Guide: Go beyond the results and understand the science behind them. Explore an extensive collection of accessible learning resources covering Earth system phenomena, scientific datasets, statistical methods, and the interpretation of results, with references to authoritative NASA and NOAA sources.
  • MCP Server: Extend Revealiã beyond its own interface through an open, free Model Context Protocol server. Compatible AI assistants can connect directly to its scientific capabilities, retrieve Earth science data, and execute analytical tools using computed results rather than relying on AI-generated guesses.

How it works

At the heart of Revealiã is a deliberate separation between scientific reasoning and numerical computation: AI decides what to investigate, while code computes every number. The agent determines which tools, datasets, and analytical methods are appropriate, but cannot invent or manually supply statistical results. Every numerical finding is populated directly from a computation performed by the system, keeping conclusions grounded in actual data.

Its analytical capabilities include:

  • Trend detection: Theil-Sen slope estimation and Mann-Kendall trend testing, accounting for year-to-year autocorrelation.
  • Regression analysis: Least-squares regression with autocorrelation correction to evaluate long-term changes.
  • Before-and-after analysis: Statistical comparisons across a specified year to investigate changes between two periods.
  • Event analysis: Compare selected months of a particular year against the same months across historical years.
  • Lagged correlation: Examine relationships between variables and identify correlations that emerge over different time lags.
  • Evidence cross-validation: Compare findings across independent data sources and cross-check satellite-derived measurements against nearby NOAA weather stations.For country- and region-level investigations, Revealiã identifies sampling locations within actual geographic boundaries and uses area-based weighting to aggregate results. Every investigation retains its data provenance, including source information, DOI, and retrieval time. Findings can be exported as detailed PDF case files or as the underlying CSV datasets for independent examination and reproducibility.

Benefits and intended impact

NASA and NOAA provide enormous amounts of openly available Earth science data, but accessing, processing, analysing, and interpreting it often requires specialised knowledge and technical skills. Revealiã brings these stages together in one accessible platform, removing much of the technical friction that prevents students, educators, and the public from engaging with scientific data.

By making real scientific investigations accessible without requiring accounts, manual downloads, or specialised software, Revealiã helps users move beyond simply consuming scientific information to actively investigating it. Students can explore environmental changes, distinguish meaningful trends from normal year-to-year variation, and develop a better understanding of how scientific evidence is evaluated.

Investigations can also be shared through links, exported as PDF case files, and downloaded as CSV datasets, making findings easier to communicate, revisit, and independently examine.

Scientific integrity is central to this goal. When the evidence is inconclusive, Revealiã communicates that the available data cannot establish a clear change rather than claiming nothing happened. It also distinguishes observed trends from causal explanations, helping users develop a more critical understanding of scientific findings.

Our intended impact is to lower the barrier to Earth science investigation and empower more people to explore, understand, and independently examine changes happening across our planet.

Tools and technology

  • Frontend: Built with vanilla JavaScript, HTML, and CSS without a specific framework or build step. This allows the same statistical implementation to run in both the browser and MCP server. Apache ECharts powers data visualisations, alongside a custom WebGL-based interactive globe.
  • Backend and hosting: Cloudflare Workers provides serverless execution, supported by Cloudflare D1 for database storage and KV for caching and shareable investigations.
  • AI orchestration: Anthropic Claude, integrated through its official SDK, powers the tool-calling investigation agent.
  • AI interoperability: The official Model Context Protocol server library exposes Revealiã's scientific capabilities to compatible AI assistants.
  • Scientific data: NASA Giovanni and GES DISC datasets, including GPM IMERG, MERRA-2, GLDAS, GRACE, AIRS, and OMI; NASA POWER, MODIS, GISTEMP, and GIBS; NOAA ERSST and weather station observations; and Natural Earth geographic boundaries.

Creativity and innovation

Revealiã reimagines how AI can be used for scientific investigation. Rather than treating AI as an oracle, it acts as the investigator while deterministic code handles all numerical computation. The AI interprets questions, discovers datasets, coordinates analytical tools, and guides investigations, with every numerical finding grounded in actual computation.

Its open MCP server extends these capabilities to other AI assistants, allowing them to access scientific data and execute analytical tools rather than generate unsupported numbers.

By combining AI-driven investigation, reliable computation, interactive exploration, and open interoperability, Revealiã turns AI from something that merely talks about science into something that actively helps people investigate it.

Factors considered

Scientific reliability, evidence quality, accessibility, and user privacy guided the design of Revealiã.

  • Statistical integrity: We account for year-to-year autocorrelation in trend testing and apply multiple-testing corrections when investigating several variables or locations, reducing the risk of misleading statistical conclusions.
  • Evidence independence: Different datasets may share underlying observational inputs. We distinguish genuine independent confirmation from simple consistency between sources. Findings supported by only one source are labelled "a lead, not a settled result".
  • Scientific transparency: We distinguish the absence of statistically clear evidence from evidence that no change occurred. Trends are not presented as proof of causation, and limitations are communicated rather than concealed.
  • Accessibility: The platform is designed to work across devices, including phones, with plain-language explanations and no account or login requirements.
  • Privacy: Investigations can be conducted without providing names or creating accounts. Users are informed about how their questions and usage information are handled.
